Let \(f\) be the function defined over \(]-∞ ; 0 [\) by: \(f(x) = - 2 x - 4 - \ln(- x)\).

So we have \(f = v - \ln(u)\) where, for any real \(x\) in \(]-∞ ; 0 [\), \(u{\left(x \right)} = - x\)   and   \(v{\left(x \right)} = - 2 x - 4\).

The aim of the exercise is to evaluate step by step the limit of \(f\) at -∞.
